Moveset

Tap a slot, then a move. Only compatible unlocked moves are listed.

Settings

Sky Battle tilt steering

Tilt left/right to turn, forward/back to dive/climb. Calibrate while holding the phone how you play.

Cloud save (Game Jolt)

Sign in with Game Jolt to keep your progress on any device or new file version.

Move effect style

Solid = clear, solid-coloured effects. Glow = bright light effects. The game reloads to apply.

Game speed

Fast: quicker movement and basic moves, shorter stun. Big moves stay the same. Online always uses Normal.

Battle text

Minimal hides reaction words like Clash or Deflect but keeps useful info (Super effective, Protected…). Off hides all pop-up words.

Language
Opponent difficulty

Harder opponents telegraph their attacks for less time and aim ahead of you.

Time limit

When time runs out, the fighter with more HP left (as a share of their total) wins.

Battle length

How much HP each fighter starts with.

Arena
Arena Hazard

Battle Royale / custom-room style. Off = none. Random picks one each fight. Thunderstorm / Cyclone / Hell Blizzard hit the whole arena.

Graphics

High adds glow and lens effects. The game switches to Low by itself if it runs slowly.

Camera

Far and Very far show more of the arena around you.

Music
Sound effects
Move sound test

Tap a move to hear its sound effect.

Controls and rules
  • Move with the left side of the screen. Tap a move to auto-aim at your target, or drag from the move button to aim it yourself, then release. Release on the red pill at the top to cancel.
  • Blue shapes on the ground show where your attack will land. Red shapes are your opponent's attack about to land; step out of them, jump, or dodge.
  • Energy powers Jump (15) and Dodge (25). Guard is free to hold but costs energy for every hit it blocks; an empty bar breaks your guard. Energy refills on its own while you stand still, and Charge refills it fast for up to 3 seconds while you stay put.
  • Keyboard: WASD move, 1–4 moves, Space jump, Shift dodge, hold F guard, R charge, Q lock on, Esc pause.
  • Jump clears ground shockwaves like Earthquake and Surf. Big moves have longer cooldowns.
  • Held items: tap the item button under your Pokémon in the selection screen. Mega Stones unlock Mega Evolution, a Z-Crystal unlocks Z-Moves of its type, and the Dynamax Band unlocks Dynamax. Other items include Focus Sash, Leftovers, Life Orb, Choice items, Expert Belt, Assault Vest, Rocky Helmet, Sitrus Berry, and Lum Berry.
  • Story Mode: your Pokémon use only what's in your bag. Buy items, Mega Stones, Z-Crystals, and TMs in the Shop, then set held items and moves on the Pokémon screen.
  • Status moves like Swords Dance, Dragon Dance, and Calm Mind raise your stats for the rest of the battle, up to +6. Recover and Roost restore HP. Some attacks also raise or lower stats; the chips on each HP panel show current changes.
  • Mega Evolution: once per battle, Pokémon that can Mega Evolve get a rainbow Mega Evolve button (or M). It boosts their stats for 30 seconds, then they return to normal.
  • Dynamax: when the gold ring is full you can Dynamax instead of using a Z-Move (button or X), once per battle. You grow giant for 20 seconds with 35% more HP, shrug off flinching, and your moves become Max Moves. A Pokémon can't Dynamax while Mega Evolved.
  • Z-Move: the gold ring fills as you deal and take damage. When it glows, tap Burst (or E) for your type's ultimate attack, a huge area strike at your opponent.
  • Perfect dodge: dodge just before a hit lands to slow time, regain energy, and charge Burst. Parry: start guarding just before a hit to block it completely and stun close-range attackers.
  • Status: fire can burn, electric can paralyze, ice can freeze, and poison poisons. Big moves also leave terrain behind: burning ground, electric fields, ice, sludge, and puddles. Electric moves hit 30% harder on anyone standing in water.
  • Single Battle can be 1 vs 1, 3 vs 3, or 6 vs 6. Pick your whole team before the battle; there is no switching. When a Pokémon faints the next one is sent out, and the winner keeps fighting with whatever HP, energy, and Burst it has left. Tap during the trainer intro to skip ahead.
  • Charge moves like Solar Beam, Hyper Beam, Fire Blast, Focus Blast, and Shadow Ball: hold the move button longer to make them bigger and stronger. Hyper Beam, Giga Impact, and Roar of Time need a moment to recharge afterwards. Some moves hit several times, some can make the opponent flinch, and Dynamic Punch and Hurricane can cause confusion, which reverses your movement and can make you hurt yourself.
  • Each arena boosts one type by 20%. Combos deal a little less damage the longer they run.
  • Flying types can fly: hold Jump (or Space) to rise, up to about three jumps high, while draining energy. Let go to glide slowly down while you steer; hold again to climb. Ground shockwaves can't reach you in the air.
  • The arena has a river through the middle (it slows you, splashes, and makes you wet, so Electric moves hurt more), boulders you can jump onto that block movement, beams, and projectiles, plus patches of grass and rocky ground. Charging into a boulder stops your dash.

    Credits

    Pokémon Rumble (version 2.0.0-beta) is a free, non-profit, fan-made game created for fun. It is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by Nintendo, Creatures Inc., GAME FREAK inc. or The Pokémon Company. No money is made from it.

    Main developer
    MYS Studio: game design, development, story and testing.
    Pokémon franchise
    Pokémon was created by Satoshi Tajiri, with Ken Sugimori and Junichi Masuda, at GAME FREAK. Pokémon and all related names, characters and music are © and ™ Nintendo, Creatures Inc., GAME FREAK inc. and The Pokémon Company. Thank you to everyone behind the games, anime and cards.
    Music
    Battle music: Pokémon the Series: XYZ theme, used as a fan tribute. Menu music: a Pokémon-inspired track used as a fan tribute (original source unknown; if this is your work, please contact MYS Studio to be credited). All rights belong to The Pokémon Company and its composers and performers.
    Pokémon sprites, portraits and emoji
    PMD Sprite Collab and its community artists (sprites.pmdcollab.org). Battle sprites, faces and Pokémon emoji all come from their work; each Pokémon's page lists the artists who drew it.
    3D Pokémon models
    Pokémon 3D API asset collection (github.com/Pokemon-3D-api). Models © The Pokémon Company.
    Trainer avatars and type icons
    Pokémon Showdown (play.pokemonshowdown.com), by the Smogon and Pokémon Showdown community. Nemona (Masters) sprite by kyledove.
    Move sound effects
    Pokémon attack sound effects collected by BellBlitzKing (Pokémon SFX: Gen 1 to Gen 7 Attack Moves Collection). Sounds © The Pokémon Company, Nintendo and GAME FREAK.
    Cries and item icons
    PokéAPI cries and sprites repositories (pokeapi.co) and their contributors.
    Pokédex artwork and entries
    Official Pokémon artwork and Pokédex text via PokéAPI and its sprites repository. Artwork © The Pokémon Company.
    Pokémon data
    Stats, types, learnsets and the damage formula follow the main series games, with learnset data from Pokémon Showdown.
    Title artwork
    Supplied by MYS Studio for this project.
    Made for this game
    Bond stories (retelling Pokémon legends from the games and Pokédex), avatar frames, the ₽ coin, reward screens, and the Bahasa Melayu and Bahasa Indonesia translations.
    Sound effects
    Generated live in the browser with the Web Audio API.
    Engine and libraries
    three.js with GLTFLoader and DRACOLoader (MIT), Draco 3D decoder by Google (Apache 2.0), PeerJS (MIT), MQTT.js (MIT), JSZip (MIT). Fonts: Barlow and Barlow Condensed (SIL Open Font License) via Google Fonts.
    Online services
    Game Jolt API (login and scores), PeerJS server (connecting players for online battles) and the HiveMQ public broker (online lobby list).
    Built with
    Claude by Anthropic, and Grok by xAI.
